quiz.question_id: Masalah inti dari pola `go process(item)` untuk setiap item besar adalah...
quiz.question_en: The core problem with the pattern `go process(item)` for every item in a large list is...
options_id: Jumlah goroutine bisa tumbuh tak terbatas dan penggunaan resource menjadi tidak terkontrol
Setiap goroutine otomatis diblok oleh compiler
Hasil jadi selalu berurutan
Channel tidak bisa dipakai lagi
options_en: The goroutine count can grow without bound and resource usage becomes uncontrolled
Each goroutine is automatically blocked by the compiler
Results become strictly ordered
Channels can no longer be used

quiz.question_id: Apa manfaat utama jumlah worker yang tetap pada worker pool?
quiz.question_en: What is the main benefit of having a fixed number of workers in a worker pool?
options_id: Membatasi concurrency sehingga penggunaan resource lebih terkontrol
Menjamin hasil selalu urut
Menghapus kebutuhan akan `WaitGroup`
Membuat semua jobs selesai dalam satu iterasi
options_en: It bounds concurrency so resource usage is more controlled
It guarantees results are always ordered
It removes the need for a `WaitGroup`
It makes all jobs finish in one iteration

quiz.question_id: Mengapa fungsi worker melakukan `for job := range jobs`?
quiz.question_en: Why does the worker function use `for job := range jobs`?
options_id: Agar worker terus memproses job sampai channel `jobs` ditutup
Agar worker hanya memproses satu job
Agar `results` tertutup otomatis
Agar tidak perlu `WaitGroup`
options_en: So the worker keeps processing jobs until the `jobs` channel is closed
So the worker processes only one job
So `results` closes automatically
So no `WaitGroup` is needed

quiz.question_id: Mengapa `close(jobs)` penting setelah semua pekerjaan dikirim?
quiz.question_en: Why is `close(jobs)` important after all work has been sent?
options_id: Agar worker tahu tidak ada job lagi dan dapat keluar dari loop range
Agar memori channel langsung dibebaskan
Agar `wg.Done()` dipanggil otomatis oleh runtime
Agar hasil menjadi terurut
options_en: So workers know there are no more jobs and can exit the range loop
So channel memory is immediately freed
So `wg.Done()` is automatically called by the runtime
So results become ordered

options_id: Agar `WaitGroup` sudah mencatat worker sebelum ia mungkin selesai dan memanggil `Done()`
Agar worker bisa membaca `jobs` lebih cepat
Agar channel `results` menjadi buffered
Karena `Add` hanya boleh dipakai di goroutine utama
options_en: So the `WaitGroup` has already counted the worker before it might finish and call `Done()`
So the worker can read `jobs` faster
So the `results` channel becomes buffered
Because `Add` may only be used in the main goroutine

quiz.question_id: Mengapa `results` ditutup di goroutine terpisah setelah `wg.Wait()`?
quiz.question_en: Why is `results` closed in a separate goroutine after `wg.Wait()`?
options_id: Agar goroutine utama tetap bisa range membaca hasil saat worker masih berjalan
Agar worker bisa menulis ke channel yang sudah tertutup
Karena `wg.Wait()` wajib dijalankan di goroutine terpisah
Untuk mengurutkan output berdasarkan ID
options_en: So the main goroutine can keep ranging over results while workers are still running
So workers can write to a channel that is already closed
Because `wg.Wait()` must run in a separate goroutine
To sort output by ID

quiz.question_id: Apa bahaya jika `results` ditutup sebelum semua worker selesai mengirim hasil?
quiz.question_en: What is the danger if `results` is closed before all workers finish sending?
options_id: Worker yang masih mengirim ke channel tertutup dapat menyebabkan panic
Hasil otomatis di-buffer ke disk
`jobs` akan ikut tertutup otomatis
`WaitGroup` akan menambah counter sendiri
options_en: A worker still sending to a closed channel can cause a panic
Results are automatically buffered to disk
`jobs` is automatically closed too
The `WaitGroup` increments its counter by itself

quiz.question_id: Mengapa lesson mencatat bahwa urutan hasil bisa bervariasi?
quiz.question_en: Why does the lesson note that result order may vary?
options_id: Karena beberapa worker berjalan konkuren dan menyelesaikan job pada waktu berbeda
Karena channel `results` selalu mengurutkan secara acak
Karena `WaitGroup` membalik urutan hasil
Karena Go melarang output berurutan di concurrency
options_en: Because multiple workers run concurrently and finish jobs at different times
Because the `results` channel always sorts randomly
Because the `WaitGroup` reverses result order
Because Go forbids ordered output in concurrency

quiz.question_id: Pada versi dengan context, apa tujuan case `<-ctx.Done()` di worker?
quiz.question_en: In the context-aware version, what is the purpose of the `<-ctx.Done()` case in the worker?
options_id: Menghentikan worker lebih awal saat ada cancellation atau timeout
Mengosongkan channel `jobs`
Mengganti `WaitGroup`
Mengubah worker menjadi sender ke `jobs`
options_en: To stop the worker early when there is cancellation or timeout
To empty the `jobs` channel
To replace the `WaitGroup`
To turn the worker into a sender on `jobs`

quiz.question_id: Untuk jenis pekerjaan mana lesson secara eksplisit menyarankan worker pool?
quiz.question_en: For which kind of work does the lesson explicitly suggest a worker pool?
options_id: Pemrosesan banyak file, scraping URL, API calls konkuren, batch DB, atau image resizing
Hanya render template HTML tunggal
Hanya parsing satu string kecil
Hanya operasi yang harus berurutan ketat
options_en: Processing many files, URL scraping, concurrent API calls, DB batch work, or image resizing
Only rendering a single HTML template
Only parsing one small string
Only operations that must be strictly sequential
